annotation.summary_en: A soldier returns from the army to discuss marriage with his father, only to discover that every local girl he likes is actually his half-sister due to his father's 'hard work' with the neighbors.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch begins in a domestic setting where a young man in a military uniform returns home from his service. He is greeted with extreme excitement by his father and a female family member (played by a male comedian in drag), who fuss over how thin he has become. Once they settle in a room filled with bookshelves, the father encourages his son to get married and asks if he has a sweetheart. The son mentions Luso, the daughter of a neighbor named Sirush. The father dejectedly explains that during the Soviet era, he was very 'hardworking' and spent his nights at Sirush's house while her husband was away; therefore, Luso is the son's half-sister. The son then suggests Vardushik, another neighbor's daughter, but the father repeats the same story about his 'hardworking' nature at that house too, revealing she is also a half-sister. Finally, the mother (played by a male comedian in drag) enters and tells the boy he can marry whoever he wants because those girls aren't actually his sisters—revealing through a final punchline that she was also quite 'hardworking' in her youth, implying the son is not the father's biological child.
catchphrases: Որովհետև տղա ջան, ջահել ժամանակ ես էլ նենց ոչինչ աշխատասեր աղջիկ էի
